analysis:
The PR adds one key, the literal "DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED", to LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (head lines 276-279 comment, line 295 entry). A new test, forwardsGDNPromptKernelRollbackToProviderJob, covers the forwarding. The base and head text of LaunchAgent.swift are otherwise identical.

Security behavior:
- The allowlist is still explicit. passthroughEnvironment (head 327-348) forwards only allowlisted, non-empty keys, so arbitrary shell environment variables still do not reach the launchd plist. The test asserts UNRELATED_SECRET is excluded.
- The new variable selects a Qwen GDN prompt-kernel mode (stock vs. packed/rows). It is a performance and rollback lever and does not touch the transport, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, or the cache's at-rest posture. Its mode parsing lives in MLXLLM, which I did not see.
- An operator who controls their own plist and environment could already set this value locally. That is within ADV-001's existing capabilities (T-013/T-014 class) and does not change the trust model.
- The change does not touch the prefix cache (T-041), the SSD tier, the TTL, or the HMAC naming, so that threat's posture is unchanged.
- WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys is intentionally left without the key. The test asserts this, which avoids widening the watchdog's environment surface (T-043).
- Residual unverified contract: whether an unexpected GDN kernel mode in the provider job could change numerical outputs is outside the supplied evidence. This relates to T-007/T-056, where the operator is already an adversary of output correctness. Nothing in this diff shows a regression.

No threat-model update is needed beyond the existing coverage.
